analyticalQuestion: How does shrinking the observation layer change the certified strong-coupling phase region, and what exact root growth survives inside that layer?
takeaway: Local quadratic exposure enlarges the certified decay region from alpha<6/7 at fixed layer length to alpha<3/2 when the layer shrinks sufficiently fast. An exact one-carrier bilateral lattice still carries a selected Bessel root mass asymptotic to (8/pi^2) log R inside a layer of order R^-3, so coupling dependence cannot be removed entirely.
palettePolicy: one muted blue root plus one ochre focus and neutral references
nonColorEncoding: panel order from theorem region to exact family to scale diagnostics

panels.A: certified alpha boundary against layer exponent beta
panels.B: producer and independent selected-root mass against the exact frozen Bessel sum and logarithmic asymptote
panels.C: physical observation-layer length and maximum physical exact-root displacement with R^-3 and R^-6 guides

claimBoundary: Panels A and the reference curves are analytic formulas. Producer and independent markers are deterministic finite bilateral-lattice calculations. The Bessel theorem is proved on the infinite bilateral lattice, while finite calculations only corroborate it. G is the rescaled-time row mass sum |P0 V F|^2 at selected positive target roots; it is not divided by Omega^2. The family has one carrier, does not establish a normalized nonlinear Navier-Stokes lower bound, is not DNS, and proves no regularity or blow-up statement.
